_doc: Forge V2 WAVE B / B2 (2026-07-18) — SHIPPED, product-owned standing rules (2026-09-26: split from owner-added state per external audit N4/P1 — see forge-standing.cjs's file header for the full split/migration contract). Read only via .claude/forge-bin/forge-standing.cjs::match()/listActive() — no other file may re-implement scope/trigger matching (same 'single source of truth, no parallel regex/logic' discipline forge-actiongate.cjs::classify established for hard-gates.json). Advisory, not a hook — matches this project's light-security governance (CLAUDE.md: 'no mandatory security gates'). Every rule here is grounded in evidence that SHIPS WITH THE PRODUCT (this project's own root CLAUDE.md, a shipped skill/command file, or the Bash tool's own Git Safety Protocol) — never a citation to a file absent on a fresh install. NOTHING here is fabricated or inferred-as-fact; any inferred operationalization (e.g. attaching a concrete glob to a general policy sentence, or generalizing a domain-specific shipped doctrine line) is marked confidence:'medium' and explained in that rule's 'notes'. This file is NEVER auto-written by reflection/distillation — B3's forge-reflect may only stage 'proposed' candidates elsewhere. OWNER-added rules (an explicit '/forge remember') live in the SEPARATE, never-shipped FORGE_STANDING_RULES.user.json — forge-standing.cjs::load() merges both transparently; remember() writes ONLY to the user file; a rule with source 'owner /forge remember' ever found HERE is migrated (moved, not copied) into the user file on the next load(). The 'honesty-core-untouchable' rule carries cannot_override_core:true and can never be shadowed or disabled by any other rule, including a higher-precedence scope/trigger match — forge-standing.cjs::match() enforces this mechanically, not just by convention.

rules.text: Never claim a check/test/review ran if it didn't. Always report what was installed/changed, which files, which agents/skills ran, which checks actually ran, and what was not run.
rules.source: CLAUDE.md (this project's root, section 'Honesty (REQUIRED)') — verbatim: "Never claim a check/test/review ran if it didn't. Always report: what was installed/changed, which files, which agents/skills ran, which checks actually ran, and what was not run."
rules.notes: The engine invariant: this rule may be REINFORCED but never weakened, shadowed, or disabled by any other rule regardless of scope specificity — enforced by forge-standing.cjs::match(), not just documentation.

rules.text: Forge works only in this project folder. Never edit other projects or unrelated directories.
rules.source: CLAUDE.md (this project's root, section 'Project isolation (REQUIRED — always on)', item 1) — verbatim: "Only this folder. Forge works only in *this* project folder. Never edit other projects or unrelated directories."

rules.text: Never push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so.
rules.source: Bash tool description, 'Git Safety Protocol' (the environment's own governing tool policy) — verbatim: "DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks to do so."

rules.text: Outreach (SMS, outbound calls, cold email, marketing sends) stays draft-only unless the owner explicitly approves sending.
rules.source: commands/forge.md (this project's shipped BEGINNER PROMISE section) — verbatim: "It stops for the hard gates — deploy, push, spend, DNS, production, credentials, activating a live workflow, sending anything out, killing processes by name, ... — ... and for a real usage-limit pause."
rules.notes: confidence:medium reflects the operationalization only (forge.md's 'sending anything out' hard gate generalized to a standing-rule sentence) — kept as the GLOBAL fallback for this topic; the more specific scraping-domain wording below (a direct verbatim quote from a shipped skill) is expected to shadow this one whenever type=scraping (same topic, higher-precedence trigger).

rules.text: Outreach is drafted-only unless the owner explicitly approves sending.
rules.source: skills/forge-scraping/SKILL.md (this project's shipped scraping playbook), line 12 — verbatim: "Outreach is DRAFTED ONLY. No automatic sending and no bulk outreach without explicit user confirmation and a compliance check."

rules.text: Real content (no lorem/placeholder), responsive desktop + tablet + mobile, working nav/forms/search with loading + empty + error states, zero console errors, accessibility basics, intentional non-template design, and a screenshot check before calling it done.
rules.source: skills/forge-website/SKILL.md (this project's shipped website playbook), lines 11-12 — verbatim: "Mobile and desktop layout verified by screenshot before claiming done." / "No placeholder/Lorem/test/mock content in anything headed for prod."
rules.notes: confidence:medium reflects the operationalization only — the rule text broadens the two shipped skill lines (screenshot check + no placeholder content) into the fuller website-quality checklist this project already applies; the two quoted lines are the direct, high-confidence shipped evidence.

rules.text: Never commit secrets, credentials, or .env files.
rules.source: CLAUDE.md (user-global, 'Ruflo — Claude Code Configuration', section 'Rules') — verbatim: "NEVER commit secrets, credentials, or .env files."
rules.notes: confidence:medium reflects the inferred glob-scope mapping only — the rule TEXT itself is a direct, high-confidence verbatim quote; the '**/.env*' glob is Build Boss's reasonable operationalization of that text, not a glob the owner literally specified.

rules.text: Codex stays available as an optional code-quality review for important changes. If Codex isn't available, don't block — just report it wasn't run.
rules.source: CLAUDE.md (this project's root, section 'Codex (optional reviewer)') — verbatim: "Codex stays available as an optional code-quality review for important changes (codex-reviewer agent → /codex:review). If Codex isn't available, don't block — just report it wasn't run."

rules.text: Forge runs commands, scripts, installs and builds itself and never asks the user to run a file or code; it does not ask 'shall I continue?' between phases — only a hard gate or a real usage-limit pause interrupts.
rules.source: commands/forge.md (this project's shipped BEGINNER PROMISE section) — verbatim: "Forge does it for you. It runs every command, script, install and build itself and never asks the user to run a file or code ... It never asks 'shall I continue?' / 'moet ik verder?' between phases (autonomy continue-within-mission, start-gate off, standing rule does-it-for-you)."
rules.notes: Originates in an owner /goal directive (2026-09-24); re-sourced 2026-09-26 to the shipped commands/forge.md wording (which already names this exact standing rule) after an external audit found the old citation pointed at an unshipped scratch transcript no fresh install carries.
